entries.label: seal
entries.title: Walther de Hunebourg, seal on Strasbourg act 3 AST 3 I/58
entries.source: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1TbwH9ZVipu7pHB2nWRlEFbSmdTvPJOFa/view — Seal image: https://sigilla.irht.cnrs.fr/iiris_img/private/image/3%20AST%203%20I%20-%2058-sc3.png. Sigilla record for Walther de Hunebourg's 1248 seal: https://sigilla.irht.cnrs.fr/103056. The two outward-facing swan necks are in the helmet crest; the shield itself is divided per fess and does not bear the swan pair.

entries.label: armorial
entries.title: Gatschet, Wappenbuch des alten und neuen Adels der Schweiz
entries.source: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1j8nWuK7Jlag1GTBosfpkjrloO7-VemKS/view — Digitized page: https://d50941855555d8299b8bd09578b8b5b4.ds11s3ns.swisscom.com/dfg/Mss_h_h_XIV_58_master/Mss_h_h_XIV_58_p11.JPG. Zürich-section armorial image showing a blue shield with two outward-facing silver swan necks and heads. The handwritten caption most likely reads Schwandegg; Schwanegg remains possible. The secondary catalog attributes the paired-head arms to von Schwandegg of Zürich and cites Gatschet (1799), but it may rely on this same page, so the exact bearer and its connection to the medieval lords of Schwandegg remain uncertain.

entries.title: Unterschüpf Evangelical church, Rosenberg arms on the pulpit
entries.source: Earlier close-up: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1ulKwyxqYvv_pumxobTFGgjur3nGEe0Tj/view. Pulpit photograph: MJ200506, 24 February 2024, CC BY 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/): https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Evangelische_Kirche_in_Unterschüpf_067.jpg Dating: Kultur in Kirchen explicitly dates the stone pulpit to 1617 ("Die steinerne Kanzel stammt ebenfalls aus dem Jahr 1617"), citing Dehio Baden-Württemberg I (1993), p. 796: https://kulturkirchen.com/kirchen/evangelische-kirche-unterschuepf-boxberg-unterschuepf/. Helmut Neumaier, Der Reichsritter Wolf Heinrich von Ega zu Ober- und Unterschüpf, Württembergisch Franken 100 (2021), pp. 64, 66 (https://doi.org/10.53458/wfr.v100i.817), states that the stone pulpit was erected for the Reformation centenary and bears the arms of the joint local and church lords Rosenberg, Stetten, and Dienheim, with Dienheim in the central position.

entries.title: Niederstetten St Jakob, memorial of the children Reichart and Rofina von Rosenberg

entries.title: Gochsheim St Michael, epitaph of Karl Friedrich von Erthal
entries.label: effigy
entries.source: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1GDbDM7Ejd3MyeLT-bYWF3qlQ0MBoAIt4/view — https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Gochsheim_St._Michael_007.jpg — Photo by Tilman2007, CC BY 3.0. entries.title: Essingen St Wendelinuskapelle, Rosenberg swan-neck arms on north-wall mural
entries.source: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1XEv41QppispFKT2pHL_JTnxPUC83p-tu/view — Heimatverein St. Wendelinus Essingen, north-wall mural photograph, original filename Wendelinus_Nordwand_2-1889x2048.jpg: https://heimatverein-st-wendelinus-essingen.de/wp-content/uploads/2024/05/Wendelinus_Nordwand_2-1889x2048.jpg. The Heimatverein identifies the swan-neck forms left of the sacrament niche as the Rosenberg arms of Balthasar von Rosenberg: https://heimatverein-st-wendelinus-essingen.de/wandmalereien-im-altarraum/. Joachim Glatz dates the choir-tower mural cycle to around 1470 (Mittelalterliche Wandmalerei in der Pfalz und in Rheinhessen, 1981, p. 106): https://digi.ub.uni-heidelberg.de/diglit/glatz1981/0134. Glatz describes the north/south biblical scenes and west-wall Adoration of the Magi (p. 197) but does not identify Balthasar or Rosenberg arms: https://digi.ub.uni-heidelberg.de/diglit/glatz1981/0225/text_ocr. The catalog date range 1470-1546 is a working range; Glatz dates the cycle around 1470, while a 1546 document records Balthasar's settlement of roof-repair costs and says nothing about mural work: https://digi.ub.uni-heidelberg.de/diglit/glasschroeder1903/0198. The Heimatverein's Balthasar identification conflicts with the c.1470 cycle date; its local timeline places him as lord by 1530 and gives his death as 1554: https://heimatverein-st-wendelinus-essingen.de/aus-der-essinger-dorfgeschichte/. Another secondary source gives 1552: https://www.eberhard-ref.net/pf%C3%A4lzer-pers%C3%B6nlichkeiten/litera-r/rh-ry/. Whether the heraldic/figural detail is a later layer or a mistaken identification remains unresolved. The source photo's photographer and reuse license are unstated.

entries.title: Schloss Unterschüpf
Schloss Unterschüpf
Boxberg castle, building memorial of Jörg von Rosenberg and Osanna von Rosenberg, née von Eycholtzheim
entries.label: effigy
entries.source: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1l7DObHTunxziPyv02CPrQbt-rTLxD41j/view — Description supplied by the user: Two separate figure stones, 1493, commemorating the rebuilding begun in 1480. Originally outside the chapel at Boxberg castle, above a gate; since 1856 in Karlsruhe, Landessammlungen, stone hall, museum nos. C 101 and C 102. Approximately life-sized reliefs on tomb-like slabs, made during their lifetimes. Jörg wears a knee-length coat and hat and carries an axe and rosary. Osanna carries a rosary, bottle, handled basket with bread(?) and double basket-covered bottle. The editors identify these as a building memorial. Original image filename: C 00101-C 00102_D 4988.jpg.

entries.label: effigy
entries.title: Beckstein St Kilian, monument of Martin Hund von Wenkheim and Philips Hardtman von Merlau
entries.source: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1-OHlLQXyD5SWzYluCyzPyZpU2AzBAUno/view — Front photograph supplied by the user, 205 × 425 pixels; source identified by the user as FNWeb, “Wechselvolle Geschichte der Kirche”: https://www.fnweb.de/orte/lauda-koenigshofen_artikel,-lauda-koenigshofen-wechselvolle-geschichte-der-kirche-_arid,784783.html. Article blocked automated access when checked; original photographer and higher-resolution image remain unverified. https://drive.google.com/file/d/1AdAisBak__X53VFcpOYDrjqwkbApXNh4/view — Church interior photograph by Johannes Wittekind, published by the Archdiocese of Freiburg: https://www.ebfr-glocken.de/glockensuche/glocken-kirchen/?id=1462&scene_76cf73dd=detail&tab_76cf73dd=detail (image l1050692.jpg). Monument identification: Die Deutschen Inschriften, vol. 1, no. 227, p. 95, https://digi.hadw-bw.de/view/di001/0123. The catalogue dates the monument to 1558 and also records a commemoration of Philips Hardtman von Merlau, who died on 1575-06-13; it does not establish the execution date of that commemoration. The Rosenberg connection is heraldic; the reason for Merlau's commemoration on the same monument is unknown, and the smaller knight must not be assumed to be a child.
